Treaties don't pass because diplomats are persuasive. They pass because governments have no choice. The strategy creates that lack of choice.

## The Two-Track System (Bottom-Up Fear + Top-Down Paperwork)

Humans need two things to change governments: (1) terror of consequences, (2) specific paperwork to sign. The framework provides both.

**Without citizens:** Diplomats negotiate forever, politicians ignore it, the initiative dies in committee meetings.

**Without diplomacy:** Citizens protest, wave signs, go home, nothing changes.

**With both:** Citizens terrify politicians + diplomats provide an escape route = treaty passes.

This functions like a good cop / bad cop dynamic, unified under a single strategy.

## Track 1: Grassroots (Make Politicians Afraid)

### The Statistical Threshold: {{< var global_population_activism_threshold_pct >}}

[Scientists analyzed 323 political campaigns from 1900-2006](../references.qmd#3-5-rule). Finding: When {{< var global_population_activism_threshold_pct >}} of any population actively demands something, they get it. Always. No exceptions.

- [8 billion humans](../references.qmd#global-population-8-billion) × {{< var global_population_activism_threshold_pct >}} = **280 million**
- The movement requires 280 million to click YES
- There are [560 million natural allies](../references.qmd#rare-disease-patients-300m-globally)
- The math indicates this works

### Who Joins First (High-Motivation Groups)

**Rare disease patients ([300M globally](../references.qmd#rare-disease-patients-300m-globally)):** Their diseases get zero funding. They have everything to gain. Very motivated.

**Parents with sick kids ([50M+](../references.qmd#parents-of-sick-children-50m)):** Will do literally anything to save their children. Emotional intensity creates action.

**Healthcare workers ([60M globally](../references.qmd#healthcare-workers-60m-globally)):** Watch people die from bureaucracy daily. Frustrated. Want to actually cure things.

**Tech people ([100M+](../references.qmd#science-tech-community-100m)):** Understand decentralization. Hate inefficiency. See the solution clearly.

**Investors ([50M potential](../references.qmd#investment-community-50m)):** {{< var victory_bond_annual_return_pct >}} returns is compelling mathematics.

Combined: 560M potential early adopters. The strategy only needs 280M. This is called "margin of error."

### The Cell Model (Decentralized Organization)

Traditional movements have leaders, hierarchy, dues, meetings. Those fail.

This movement: Nobody's in charge. Self-organizing cells of 5-50 people. No dues (VICTORY Incentive Alignment Bonds fund it). Each cell recruits 3 more people. Cells split at 50. New cells form. It can't be shut down because there's nothing to shut down.

This is how societies got: civil rights, women's suffrage, the end of apartheid, legal weed. Works every time.

### The Recruitment Funnel (Turning Awareness Into Action)

**Stage 1 - Awareness (1 billion people):**

See message on social media. "Humans spend 40X more on killing than curing." 30-second exposure.

#### Stage 2 - Interest (500 million)

Click through. Read more. Understand the [1% treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty-academic.qmd). See personal benefit.

#### Stage 3 - Commitment (280 million)

Vote YES. Buy [VICTORY Incentive Alignment Bonds](../economics/victory-bonds-academic.qmd). Recruit others.

Conversion rates: 50% from awareness to interest, 56% from interest to commitment. Result: 280M committed from 1B aware. The math checks out.

## Track 2: Diplomatic (Providing the Administrative Framework)

### The Simultaneous Signing Strategy

#### Traditional treaty (fails)

- Country A signs first
- Country B waits to see what C does
- C wants different terms
- Takes 10 years, never happens

#### The proposed treaty (works)

- All countries sign the same day
- Nobody goes first, nobody goes last
- No advantage to waiting
- One shot, everyone commits

### Phase 1: Pilot Countries (Proof of Concept)

Target 5-10 small countries first:

- **Costa Rica:** [No military](../references.qmd#costa-rica-no-military) (easiest sell ever)
- **Nordic countries:** Already healthcare-focused
- **Singapore:** Tech-forward, pragmatic
- **New Zealand:** Progressive, willing to lead
- **Switzerland:** Neutral, humanitarian tradition

The proposition: "Be first, be heroes, minimal military impact (1%), maximum PR benefit."

### Phase 2: Major Powers (Making It Real)

Different proposition for each:

**United States:** "Lead the world in curing disease, not just weapons. Maintain military dominance (99% intact), PR victory, voters love it, [VICTORY Incentive Alignment Bonds](../economics/victory-bonds-academic.qmd) create a new financial market."

**China:** "Global leadership through health innovation. Soft power expansion. Domestic legitimacy boost."

**European Union:** "Humanitarian leadership, economic benefit, aligns with EU values, Nobel Prize territory."

**Russia:** "Security through health not just weapons. Domestic health crisis solution. International prestige."

### Phase 3: Everyone Else (Peer Pressure)

Once major powers sign, remaining countries face:

- Looking bad internationally
- Missing economic benefits
- Domestic population demanding it
- No good reason to refuse

Compliance becomes easier than resistance.

### The Minimal Ask (High Acceptance Probability)

The treaty is NOT asking for:

- Peace (they can keep fighting)
- Disarmament (they keep 99%)
- Political change
- Economic restructuring

It asks for:

- 1% budget reallocation
- That's it

So small it's hard to say no. So beneficial it's absurd to say no.

### The Enforcement (Smart Contracts)

Traditional treaties rely on good faith (fail often).

This treaty: Smart contracts + blockchain

- Automatic fund transfer
- No human discretion
- Transparent tracking
- Actually works

## Feasibility & Cost: Why This Is Realistic

A common objection is "Treaties cost billions and take forever." History proves otherwise.

The entire diplomatic campaigning and entry-into-force phase typically costs **under $25 million** (see [Ottawa Treaty precedents](../appendix/treaty-feasibility-academic.qmd)).

For a 1% Health Treaty, realistic estimates for the full campaign (negotiations, global referendum, ratification drive) are **~$90–140 million**.

See the detailed breakdown: **[Treaty Feasibility & Cost Analysis](../appendix/treaty-feasibility-academic.qmd)**.

## How The Tracks Reinforce Each Other

### Grassroots enables diplomacy

280M citizens give diplomats political cover. "Our people demand this." Creates electoral pressure. Makes refusal politically costly.

#### Diplomacy channels grassroots

Formal treaty gives citizens a concrete goal. Provides a success metric. Creates an institutional pathway. Prevents the movement from fizzling.

#### The feedback loop
```
Citizens demand treaty
    ↓
Politicians feel pressure
    ↓
Diplomats negotiate seriously
    ↓
Treaty progress announced
    ↓
More citizens join (momentum visible)
    ↓
More pressure
    ↓
More countries sign
    ↓
Positive spiral continues
```
